solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

E030-01.notes: Object of preposition 'between' needs objective case 'him'. 'he' is subjective, 'his' possessive with no noun, 'himself' has no antecedent in the same clause as subject. 'between he' tempts students who hear 'he and the site' as a compound.

E030-02.notes: Simple past of intransitive 'lie' (to recline) is 'lay'. 'laid' is the past of transitive 'lay'; 'lain' needs an auxiliary; 'lied' means told falsehoods. The lie/lay error is common, so many keep NO CHANGE.

flags: minor: answer cue - key is the only concise choice; C (redundant 'also...too') and D (passive, ungrammatical 'were') are weak distractors that few would pick
E030-03.notes: Combining into one sentence with a three-item parallel list is the most concise. A is grammatical but choppy and repetitive.

E030-04.notes: Adverb 'knowledgeably' modifies the verb 'discuss'. The adjective, the comparative and the noun all fail.

flags: minor: B, C, D are off-topic, so the item is very easy
E030-05.notes: The paragraph is about Emily going beyond being a messenger and making decisions. A transitions from her study (preceding paragraph) to that idea.

flags: C 'As a result,' is somewhat defensible: the bridge kept rising as a result of Emily making decisions. It overclaims causation, and the text frames the continuing work as concurrent rather than caused, but a reviewer should confirm D is clearly superior or reword the distractor (for example 'Nevertheless,')
E030-06.notes: The sentence about the bridge rising does not exemplify the belief that Emily made decisions, so 'For example' is wrong. 'In contrast' is not a contrast. 'Meanwhile' marks events happening at the same time, which fits work continuing as the debate over her role went on.

flags: minor: answer cue - key is the shortest; standard for ACT redundancy items
E030-07.notes: 'first person' already means before anyone else, so A, C and D are redundant. Fact check: Emily rode across first with a rooster at the May 24, 1883 opening, consistent with standard accounts.

E030-08.notes: 'Carrying a rooster...' is a participial phrase, so it must attach to the main clause with a comma. A is a fragment, B a semicolon before a non-clause, and D ('She carrying') is ungrammatical.

flags: minor: B and C are rarely chosen
E030-09.notes: Standard comma series. The comma after 'father' sets off the nonrestrictive 'who' clause. Semicolons (D) are unwarranted without internal commas. Fact check: the 1951 plaque honors Emily, Washington and John A. Roebling, so the claim is accurate.

E030-10.notes: Only D echoes the opening idea of messages flowing 'through a single person.' A, B and C are true facts but don't connect to the opening. (Construction took 14 years, it was the longest suspension bridge, and Washington died in 1926, so all distractors are factually accurate.)
